name: Zaccur
overview: Zaccur was a male Levite mentioned in the book of Nehemiah. He is specifically named among those who sealed a covenant document, indicating his active role in the religious community of post-exilic Israel. His identification as a Levite highlights his connection to the priestly tribe entrusted with temple duties.
namesAndTitles: The name Zaccur means "remembering," which is a proper Hebrew name. There is no indication that this name was given by God, but its meaning may reflect a cultural or familial emphasis on remembrance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Zaccur was a descendant of Levi, affirming his tribal heritage. He is also noted as the father of Mattaniah, with Hanan inferred as his father, establishing a three-generation lineage within the Levites.
scriptureSignificance: Zaccur's significance lies in his role as a Levite who participated in the sealing of a covenant document, demonstrating his commitment to the religious reforms and covenant renewal efforts during Nehemiah's time. His mention underscores the involvement of Levites in upholding the spiritual and communal restoration of Israel after the exile.
